properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-09 ON THIS GRAPH, ON A REAL MERGE ANTHONY AUTHORISED. `propose_heal` offered to merge the owner's two Contributor nodes and CHOSE THE WRONG SURVIVOR: keep `ctr:anthony` (8 edges, no description), destroy `who:ajs` (161 edges, the full description, and the id form `add_contributor`'s own parameter description gives as its example).

⭐ AND IT SAID SO ITSELF, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. Verbatim from `would_destroy`: "deleting 'who:ajs' keeps only 'ctr:anthony's properties; also replaced: description. THE ALPHABET CHOSE THE VICTIM: both carry the same provenance, so the smaller id survived (BL-29) — nothing about the design decided which of these two lives." The disclosure is exemplary and it is the only reason the merge was not applied as proposed. A tool that names its own arbitrariness is doing the right thing; a tool whose arbitrariness DECIDES is still wrong.

WHY THIS IS EVIDENCE AND NOT AN OPINION: `dec:merge-survivor-provenance` (ACCEPTED) says the survivor is chosen by provenance with id breaking ties. Here both nodes carry the SAME provenance, so the tie-break ran — and the tie-break is alphabetical, which has no relationship to which node the design actually depends on. `fact:defect-merge-survivor-ignores-priority-and-status` already contradicts that decision and the pair has been a standing structural defect (`heal:7456a4d260ca45ce`). THIS IS THE FIRST TIME THE DEFECT HAS BEEN OBSERVED COSTING SOMETHING ON A REAL MERGE rather than argued in the abstract.

A CHEAP SIGNAL THE RULE COULD READ, offered because naming the fix is more useful than naming the fault: EDGE COUNT. 161 against 8 is not a close call, and neither is "has a description" against "has none". Degree is already computable and would have picked correctly here without any new vocabulary. Provenance-then-alphabet is the rule that produced the wrong answer; provenance-then-degree would not have.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY DONE: the merge was performed BY HAND — `record_change` first so the snapshot holds `ctr:anthony` and all 9 of its edges, then the 8 AUTHORED_BY edges re-pointed to `who:ajs` with `role` and `acted_at` preserved and checked for pre-existing overlap (none, so nothing was overwritten), then the node deleted. `detect_defects` went 7 findings to 6 with the duplicate gone.

📝 ONE THING THIS DOES NOT SHOW, stated so the finding is not read wider than it is: `propose_heal --conservative` proposed NOTHING for this duplicate, and only `--aggressive` offered the merge. So the dangerous proposal is not the default. What the default gives instead is silence on a duplicate a human had explicitly asserted, which is its own question.
